label: Prove FTC Part 1 using the derivative definition and the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
steps: Apply the definition of the derivative to F(x).
Express the resulting difference quotient as 1/h ∫_x^{x+h} f(t)dt, the average value of f over [x,x+h].
Apply the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals to get a point c in [x,x+h] with f(c) equal to that average value.
Let h→0; since c→x and f is continuous, f(c)→f(x).
success_criteria: Derivation establishes F′(x)=f(x) for x in (a,b).
notes: Reusable proof method. The specific derivation/walkthrough is recorded separately as Study (study:proof:ftc-part1).
